candidate_relations.reason: Intestinal tuberculosis is a different infectious enteropathy, not intestinal T-cell lymphoma NOS.
Desmoid tumor is a different mass lesion and does not explain epitheliotropic lymphocytic infiltrates or perforation.
Lymphoma is the correct parent malignancy but omits intestinal T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified.
Peptic ulcer disease names the terminal-ileal perforation event rather than the underlying T-cell lymphoma.
Enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma is a related intestinal T-cell lymphoma but an incompatible WHO subtype versus lymphoma NOS; celiac disease is not established.
Crohn disease was the working inflammatory explanation for ulcers and strictures, not intestinal T-cell lymphoma NOS.
Carcinoid tumor is a different neoplasm and does not fit epitheliotropic lymphocytic infiltrates.
The truncated 'Exclusion of NK' label is not a usable diagnostic object, so relation to intestinal T-cell lymphoma NOS cannot be resolved.
NSAID-induced enteropathy is a different cause of small-bowel ulcers and is not the lymphoma.
Small-bowel adenocarcinoma is a different epithelial malignancy.
IBD was the planned outpatient diagnosis after enteroscopy and is a differential, not intestinal T-cell lymphoma NOS.
Indolent T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the GI tract is a related but incompatible indolent process versus intestinal T-cell lymphoma NOS.
GIST is a different mesenchymal tumor, not a T-cell lymphoma.
Celiac disease is an associated enteropathy in the EATL differential (atrophic duodenum) but is not intestinal T-cell lymphoma NOS.
Epithliotropic T-cell infiltrate is the histologic component that raised suspicion for lymphoma but is not the NOS lymphoma diagnosis.
Gastrointestinal lymphoma is a parent of the intestinal lymphoma but omits T-cell NOS lineage.
Scleroderma is a different systemic disease unrelated to this enteropathy-lymphoma course.
Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, intestinal type, is a related aggressive extranodal lymphoma with incompatible NK/T rather than T-cell NOS lineage.
Small-bowel obstruction is a presenting complication of strictures, not the lymphoma diagnosis.
Inflammatory bowel disease is the same competing inflammatory diagnosis as C011, not intestinal T-cell lymphoma NOS.

case_quality_flags: No complete_equivalent candidate states intestinal T-cell lymphoma NOS; C008 is a truncated non-diagnosis.
